title: The Blind Leading the Blind (The Parable of the Blind)
source: Museo di Capodimonte, Naples (public domain). Image from Wikimedia Commons: File:The Blind leading the Blind by Pieter Bruegel the Elder Google Art.jpg (6000 x 4280 px)
caption: Six men set out on a walk in 1568. Follow the line from left to right and watch closely. #blindness #bible #bruegel #fineart #hiddendetails
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-24, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blind_Leading_the_Blind): 1568, signed 'BRVEGEL.M.D.LX.VIII', distemper on linen (tüchlein), 86 x 154 cm, Museo di Capodimonte, Naples; six men; Matthew 15:14; 'The diagonal composition reinforces the off-kilter motion of the six figures falling in progression'; church resembles St Anna's in Sint-Anna-Pede (Dilbeek); medical readings by Charcot and Richer (1889), Torrilhon (1957) and Zeynel Karcioglu (2002): man 2 eyes removed, man 3 corneal leukoma, man 4 atrophy of the globe, man 5 no light perception or photophobic, man 6 pemphigus / bullous pemphigoid (counting from the leader).

VERIFIED, Matthew 15:14 wording: 'if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch' (KJV, quoted by Hektoen International, hekint.org/2021/08/30/pieter-bruegel-and-the-parable-of-the-blind/).

VERIFIED, medical study: Rutecki 2016, The Pharos (alphaomegaalpha.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/2016-1-Rutecki.pdf): enucleation, corneal leukoma, atrophy of the globes, photophobia, pemphigus; diagnoses by Charcot, Richer and Torrilhon, reviewed by ophthalmologist Karcioglu. Dates differ slightly (Torrilhon thesis 1957 vs 1958). Slide 7 says 'doctors who studied the faces have suggested', no names or dates. CAUTION: Torrilhon's claim that Bruegel must have been a physician is unproven, not used.

VERIFIED, sequence: mydailyartdisplay.uk and artinsociety.com: leader fallen on his back in the ditch, the second stumbling over him, the stick pulled forward, the rear men still unaware / alarmed by the cries. Church seen through the gap between the fourth and fifth men from the left (artinsociety.com).

CORRECTED, the cow: artinsociety.com says a small cow, a herdsman and fowl to the right of the church were 'abraded at some stage in the past' and survive only in early copies (Wikipedia still mentions a cowherd). So the slides do NOT say a cow is untroubled; slide 8 only says nobody comes to help. Good fact for comment replies.
VERIFIED, Bruegel died 9 September 1569 in Brussels (Wikipedia EN, Pieter Bruegel the Elder). NOT claimed: 'his last painting' (Wikipedia names The Storm at Sea as probably his last).
Focus boxes estimated from the contact sheet (6000x4280); retune on the real image. Least sure: the church (slide 8) and the faces for the eye conditions (slide 7).

slides.headline: Six men set out. Watch closely.
slides.sub: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Blind Leading the Blind, 1568

slides.headline: A line from Jesus
slides.text: 1568. Bruegel paints a warning from the Gospel: if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch. He takes it literally.

slides.headline: At the back, calm
slides.text: Start on the left. The last men still walk calmly, holding a shoulder or a stick, trusting whoever is in front.

slides.headline: Something's wrong
slides.text: But move right, and the mood changes. Heads lift, faces tense: the men in the middle can hear the cries ahead.

slides.headline: The stick jerks
slides.text: Then the stick they share is yanked forward. One man loses his footing, the next is already going down. A fall in slow motion.

slides.headline: The leader, in the ditch
slides.text: And at the front, the leader already lies on his back in the ditch. Everyone behind him is about to follow.

slides.headline: Look at their eyes
slides.text: Look closer at their faces. Doctors who studied them have suggested different conditions: eyes removed, a clouded white cornea, shrunken eyeballs.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, the church
slides.text: Meanwhile, through a gap in the line, a solid village church looks on, much like Sint-Anna in Pede, near Brussels. Nobody comes to help.

slides.headline: Who's leading?
slides.text: Bruegel died the next year. More than 450 years later, the warning still lands. Who do you think is leading the blind today?
